minutesRepresentation.sourceEncoding: clock-time float MM.SS: the integer part is whole minutes and the two-digit fractional part is seconds (48.53 = 48:53). The source minutes column is NOT decimal minutes.
minutesRepresentation.conversion: totalSeconds = 60 * floor(raw) + round(100 * frac(raw)); mappedMinutes = round-half-up(totalSeconds / 60) at 0.1-minute storage precision, computed in integer arithmetic ((10 * totalSeconds + 30) // 60) / 10. A raw seconds part of 60 is the encoding's own carry into the next minute (30.6 = 31:00).
minutesRepresentation.storageTolerance: mapped minutes are within 0.05 minute (3 s) of the exact decoded value; the decoded value itself matches Basketball-Reference clock readings to the second on every spot check
evidence: all 26,648 raw values at rev d480e56 have a whole-hundredth fractional part (max deviation 3.4e-13) with implied seconds in 0..60, never 61..99 as decimal hundredths would
